rows.bound_type_reason: variational ansatz at a stated size; energy is an upper bound (assigned during source reading)
rows.reference: B. Tanatar & D. M. Ceperley, Ground state of the two-dimensional electron gas, Phys. Rev. B 39, 5005 (1989), doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.39.5005

verified.method: doi:10.1103/PhysRevB.39.5005: text layer of the publisher PDF (1989 scan), every number checked against the page image at 300 dpi; no LLM transcription of numbers; single reading + page-image check
verified.note: Table I (normal fluid), row N = 42, column rs = 30; dl/tanatar-ceperley-1989.txt line 163; printed in Ry per electron; matches the page image | Energies in Ry per electron ('Energies in this paper are in units of rydbergs/electron'), converted × 1/2. Ewald sums with each electron's own images ('an electron must also interact with all of its own images which form a square lattice'): the Madelung term is included. Square simulation cell, periodic boundary conditions, plane-wave orbitals filling closed shells (Gamma). QMBL's HF check (checks/heg-hf/hf.mjs, square cell): E - E_HF per electron is -0.099 Ha at N = 26, rs = 1, -0.046 at N = 26, rs = 5, -0.0078 at N = 114, rs = 50, -0.0112 at N = 37 polarized, rs = 5 and -0.0023 at N = 113 polarized, rs = 75, close to the paper's E_c(rs) (Tables I, II); without the Madelung term the N = 26, rs = 1 energy would sit 0.216 Ha per electron higher. Every number checked against the page image (300 dpi).
